results.summary: This design is a simple blinking digit counter that drives a 7-segment display. It uses a clock input to increment a digit, which is shown on the external display. The project is implemented in Wokwi and serves as a basic test or educational example. The documentation is minimal, providing only a one-line description and pin name.

This design implements a combinational logic function that ANDs pairs of inputs and ORs the results. It takes eight inputs and produces two outputs, each representing the same logical function. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. It is a simple educational example created in Wokwi.

This design uses two inputs to display either the digit '1' or '2' on a 7-segment display. It employs AND and OR gates to control the segment outputs based on the input states. The project requires an external 7-segment display for operation. It is a simple educational example implemented in Wokwi.

This design decodes a 4-bit input into a decimal number displayed on a 7-segment display. It takes four input pins and drives the segments accordingly. The project requires an external 7-segment display. It is a basic educational design created in Wokwi, with limited documentation.

This design is a 4-bit counter that increments by 1 at approximately 1 Hz, using a clock divider from a 10 kHz input. The counter value is output on four pins and can be displayed on an external 7-segment display. The increment amount can be set via four input pins. It is a simple educational project implemented in Wokwi.

This design is a 4-bit ripple carry adder that takes two 4-bit numbers as inputs and produces a 4-bit sum plus a carry output. It is implemented using four 1-bit full adders connected in a ripple carry configuration. The design requires no external hardware and can be tested by setting the input switches. It is a straightforward educational example created in Wokwi.

This design is a modified version of the Tiny Tapeout template, with eight inputs and eight outputs. It is intended to be tested by toggling buttons and observing outputs on a 7-segment display. The documentation indicates it is a basic test project with slight modifications. It serves as an introductory example for the platform.
